notes.title: The population system
notes.content:
[p][b]In the newly implemented system, each individual is tracked.[/b][/p][p]Every person is born, attends school, and may go on to study—sometimes for a long time, sometimes not.
Each individual belongs to a [b]social category[/b], which influences their chances of reaching higher levels of education.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45597461/140db70944127de6f1ab1a51c7780ddff2714929.png"][/img][/p][p]After completing their schooling, they begin looking for a [b]job[/b] and start working.
Children will also be born, continuing the endless cycle—unless, of course, you fail to prevent the blackout.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45597461/780b88c50488607cc30a69bb5b3057e2a6c83bbf.png"][/img][/p][p]Education at level 3 and above is specialized in one of a dozen [b]fields[/b], composed around [b]fundamental domains[/b] of knowledge.
Most of the time, people will work in the same field they studied. However, circumstances may force them to switch careers, often at the cost of losing skills—and possibly even a drop in social status. It will depends anyway of the distance between new job field and previous fields.[/p][p]During their working life, individuals can gain [b]experience[/b], and in some cases, their education level may improve.[/p][p]Both [b]companies[/b] and the [b]education system[/b] require a steady supply of people with the right qualifications. A business isn't just a matter of money—it also depends on having the right workers available.[/p][p]You'll be able to adjust key parameters, such as the [b]minimum working age[/b], [b]retirement age[/b], and the [b]educational programs[/b] offered in your various schools. Will you allow students to choose their own path, or will you tightly control which subjects are available?[/p][p]The system also factors in [b]fertility rates[/b], and [b]adult and child life expectancy[/b]—all of which can evolve over the nearly three centuries of gameplay.[/p]

notes.title: v0.13.0 Population simulator
notes.content:
A first version of a [b]population simulator[/b] has been developed. Rather than having a very artificial variation in the number of individuals, here each person is managed from birth to death. At first, I didn't think I would need so much detail. It is the future management of the [b]assignment[/b] of individuals in companies and services based on their level of education that motivated me to do it. We probably won't see people wandering the streets, but that doesn't stop me from trying to give them substance. However, individuals will have a more abstract influence than the [b]characters[/b], another key feature of the game.
